therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: NK1 receptor antagonism and 5-HT3 receptor antagonism
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Prevention of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Pediatric cancer patients receiving highly or moderately emetogenic chemotherapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Pharmacokinetic parameters (AUC0-inf and Cmax) of netupitant and exposure-response analysis

results.effect_size: AUC0-inf ranged from 2276-17340 ng*hr/mL across age groups and doses; Cmax ranged from 60.8-275 ng/mL
results.target_engagement_evidence: Measurable plasma concentrations of netupitant achieved across all age groups with dose-proportional increases
subgroup_findings: Higher netupitant exposure (4 mg/kg vs 1.33 mg/kg) achieved across all age groups
No significant exposure-response relationship (Pearson R = 0.076, p = 0.55 for AUC; R = -0.041, p = 0.75 for Cmax)
results.dose_information: Netupitant 1.33 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg oral suspension (max 100 mg or 300 mg respectively) plus Palonosetron 20 μg/kg oral solution (max 1.5 mg)

context.comparator: Dose comparison study (1.33 mg/kg vs 4 mg/kg netupitant)
context.duration: 168 hours follow-up for PK, delayed phase assessment 24-120 hours post-chemotherapy
